html:
Monte Albán was the capital of the Zapotec people in the valley of Oaxaca, in southern Mexico, founded around 500 BCE on a mountain top that its builders levelled. It was one of the first cities of Mesoamerica and was occupied for over a thousand years.

Around a great plaza stood temples, palaces and a ball court. Hundreds of carved stones called danzantes show naked, twisted men, probably slain captives, and some of the oldest writing in Mesoamerica, with early dates of the 52-year calendar. At its height the city held perhaps 25,000 people and ruled much of Oaxaca. It had ties with Teotihuacan.

It declined after about 800. Later the Mixtec reused its tombs; Tomb 7, opened in 1932, held a famous treasure of gold and jade. It became a World Heritage Site with the city of Oaxaca in 1987, alongside Chichén Itzá and the Pyramid of the Sun in Mexico.
